Designed under tight timeline; project was first part level design freeze on drivetrain
Validated over 275 miles of testing with no fatigue failures

title: 2026-27 Drivetrain Architecture
summary: Single-motor, single-reduction chain-drive RWD drivetrain for the 2027 Longhorn Racing Electric car (Emrax 228 motor, Cascadia CM200DZ inverter, Drexler LSD). I owned the architecture trade studies and drivetrain design decisions, aimed at shifting sprung mass rearward and cutting mass while staying simple to build, tune, and service.

stats.label: Car-wide CG height change from flipped inverter layout
Diff package mass, 8.49 lb to about 6.5 lb (estimate)
Rear-box mass avoided by running the diff off the back

cards.title: The problem
items: Team goals: 100 data-driven miles before unveiling and a top-5 finish at the 2027 competition
Drivetrain needs: minimal complexity, tunability, and serviceability

cards.title: Hard constraints
items: FSAE rules: diff mounts must reach the top and bottom edges of the rear bulkhead
A connected motor/diff mount counts as one non-crushable object; 100 mm battery clearance
220 Nm peak torque at 43/13, 1.5 chain shock factor, 2x safety factor
Spec for 30 endurances (410 mi): 6,500 rpm motor, 1,965 rpm diff, about 517k diff cycles

cards.title: Diff off the back
cards.decision: Selected a four-mount layout with no axial member over 3 alternatives.
cards.why: Avoids 1.38 lb (163%) of added rear-box mass, plus the extra tube weight of larger axial members and a nominal 19.68 degree halfshaft angle.

cards.title: Differential selection
cards.decision: Drexler V2 LSD with custom parts over the Quaife MK3.
cards.why: Independent accel/decel and braking tunability supports the data-driven goal. Custom parts bring the package from 8.49 lb to about 6.5 lb.

cards.title: Gear ratio: 43:13 (3.3)
cards.decision: Chose the ratio from a quasi-steady-state sweep of 75 m acceleration time and finish speed.
cards.why: A lower ratio means a smaller driven sprocket: lower bearing and sprocket loads, less mass, and tighter packaging.

cards.title: Inverter placement
cards.decision: Orion-style mount with the inverter flipped, over a floor mount (5.5 vs 4 pts across 9 criteria).
cards.why: Allows further diff position at max halfshaft angle and a narrower rear box, and the flip recovers CG (-3.95 mm) and eases mounting. Cost: a carbon-fiber mount and a separate jacking point.

cards.title: Center-driven sprocket: rejected
cards.why: Center-driven cut tab loads about 29%, but scored 0.23 vs 0.77 weighted on loading, simplicity, certainty, and failure magnitude.

cards.title: Motor mount and brake rotor
cards.decision: Triangle motor mount with the brake rotor on the preload-nut side.
cards.why: Stiffens the frame and deletes steel reinforcement tubes; avoids a cantilevered motor output shaft.

cards.title: Halfshafts and diff assembly
cards.decision: Halfshaft OD reduced from 20 to 18 mm; TRE Lightning-series tripod joint (about 25 degree max angle).
cards.why: Mass savings and CG bias outweigh the small efficiency loss, checked against joint-angle efficiency data.

cards.title: Diff mounts and chain tensioning
cards.decision: Mounts swept over two pitch lengths, with extensions in place of a slip-based adjuster.
cards.why: Continuous chain adjustment, easy to manufacture, consistent and measurable tension, and rules-compliant bulkhead tie-in.

items: 3.95 mm car-wide CG height change from the flipped inverter layout
Diff package about 23% lighter than the stock configuration
Full drivetrain scheduled for manufacture by Jan 11

note: Team context: sprocket sizing and FEA planning and the load-case and cycle calculations were developed with teammates.
